- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to short-term forecasts.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays reaction; forecast should accelerate upward by 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.  
- For long-term (10+ days) forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with actual volatility persistence.
